===== .cache/memory-views/build-binaries.py SHA256 9eb5d1b538b7030f1b93d60be2cf4d06fea45ca236e88314c6f30b2a279b4f75 =====
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib,json,os,subprocess
root=Path.cwd();out=root/'.cache/memory-views'
go='/usr/lib64/go/1.26/bin/go'
env=dict(os.environ,GOTOOLCHAIN='local',CGO_ENABLED='0',GOAMD64='v1',GOCACHE=str(root/'.cache/go'),GOFLAGS='-buildvcs=false')
records={}
for role in ['before','after','reload','stream-before','stream-after']:
 package='./testdata/streaming/go/streaming' if role.startswith('stream') else './examples/datadog/go/dd'
 overlay=out/(role+'-overlay.json')
 common=[go,'test','-pgo=off']
 if overlay.exists(): common.append('-overlay='+str(overlay))
 command=[*common,'-c','-o',str(out/(role+'.test')),package]
 identity_files=[root/(package[2:]+'/internal/wasm/module.go')]
 if overlay.exists(): identity_files=[overlay,out/(role+'-module.go')]
 record={'command':command,'cwd':str(root),'environment':{k:env[k] for k in ['GOTOOLCHAIN','CGO_ENABLED','GOAMD64','GOCACHE','GOFLAGS']},'source_identity':{str(p):hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in identity_files}}
 with (out/(role+'-build.log')).open('w') as log:
  print('COMMAND',json.dumps(command),file=log,flush=True)
  subprocess.run(command,cwd=root,env=env,stdout=log,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,check=True)
  test=[*common,package,'-count=1']
  print('COMMAND',json.dumps(test),file=log,flush=True)
  subprocess.run(test,cwd=root,env=env,stdout=log,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,check=True)
 record['binary_sha256']=hashlib.sha256((out/(role+'.test')).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
 records[role]=record
 (out/'build-records.json').write_text(json.dumps(records,indent=2)+'\n')
 print('PASS build/oracle',role,flush=True)

===== .cache/memory-views/freeze.py SHA256 5ac2a96603adfe37c5727f7a24c33d1e89cd8c6805e260b521e365d4b9e7b8fb =====
"""Record immutable qualification inputs; never build or execute benchmarks."""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os
import platform
import subprocess

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
ENV_KEYS = ("CGO_ENABLED", "GOAMD64", "GOMAXPROCS", "GOGC", "GOMEMLIMIT", "GODEBUG",
            "GOEXPERIMENT", "GOTOOLCHAIN", "GOFLAGS", "GOWORK", "GOTRACEBACK")


def path(value):
    result = Path(value)
    return result if result.is_absolute() else ROOT / result


def digest(filename):
    return hashlib.sha256(filename.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def roles(plan, leaf):
    if leaf["family"] == "stream":
        return plan["stream_roles"]
    if leaf["family"] == "guest":
        return plan["guest_roles"]
    return plan["dd_roles"]


def verify(snapshot):
    for filename, expected in snapshot["sha256"].items():
        actual = digest(Path(filename))
        if actual != expected:
            raise RuntimeError(f"frozen input changed: {filename}: {expected} -> {actual}")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("config", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    config_file = args.config.resolve()
    config = json.loads(config_file.read_text())
    plan_file = path(config["plan"])
    plan = json.loads(plan_file.read_text())
    assert len(plan["leaves"]) == 17
    selected = {role for leaf in plan["leaves"] for role in roles(plan, leaf)}
    assert selected == set(config["binaries"])
    assert selected == set(config["build_records"])
    files = {config_file, plan_file, Path(__file__).resolve(),
             path(".cache/memory-views/paired.py"), path(".cache/memory-views/summarize.py")}
    files.update(path(value) for value in config["artifacts"])
    files.update(path(value) for value in config["binaries"].values())
    # Overlay JSON identifies substituted inputs, not their contents. Freeze
    # each actual replacement too, including adapted reference harnesses.
    for filename in tuple(files):
        if filename.suffix == ".json":
            metadata = json.loads(filename.read_text())
            if isinstance(metadata, dict) and "Replace" in metadata:
                assert isinstance(metadata["Replace"], dict)
                files.update(path(value) for value in metadata["Replace"].values() if value)
    for record in config["build_records"].values():
        assert set(record) >= {"command", "cwd", "source_identity"}
        encoded = json.dumps(record)
        assert "FILL" not in encoded, "replace build-record placeholders"
        assert "-pgo=off" in encoded, "PGO-off build command missing"

    # Freeze every authored benchmark file in the two consumed packages, and
    # require byte-identical baseline source. A new harness requires rebuilding
    # the baseline too rather than silently comparing differently linked files.
    baseline_harness = {}
    for directory in ("examples/datadog/go/dd", "testdata/streaming/go/streaming"):
        for filename in sorted(path(directory).glob("*bench_test.go")):
            relative = str(filename.relative_to(ROOT))
            original = subprocess.check_output(
                ["git", "show", plan["baseline_revision"] + ":" + relative], cwd=ROOT)
            assert original == filename.read_bytes(), f"harness differs from baseline: {relative}"
            baseline_harness[relative] = hashlib.sha256(original).hexdigest()
            files.add(filename)

    # Include all current runtime/hardener Go sources, even candidate untracked
    # files, so source changes during an isolated round invalidate the freeze.
    for directory in ("rt", "internal/harden"):
        files.update(path(directory).rglob("*.go"))
    for directory in ("examples/datadog/go/dd", "testdata/compute/go/compute", "testdata/streaming/go/streaming"):
        files.update(path(directory).rglob("*.go"))
    build_info = {}
    for role, value in config["binaries"].items():
        filename = path(value)
        info = subprocess.check_output([plan["measurement_go"], "version", "-m", str(filename)], text=True)
        for required in (plan["measurement_go_version"], "CGO_ENABLED=0", "GOARCH=amd64", "GOOS=linux", "GOAMD64=v1"):
            assert required in info, (role, required, info)
        build_info[role] = info

    snapshot = {
        "utc": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "head": subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=ROOT, text=True).strip(),
        "git_status": subprocess.check_output(["git", "status", "--short"], cwd=ROOT, text=True),
        "platform": platform.platform(), "uname": list(platform.uname()),
        "affinity": sorted(os.sched_getaffinity(0)),
        "cpuinfo": Path("/proc/cpuinfo").read_text(),
        "go_version": subprocess.check_output([plan["measurement_go"], "version"], text=True).strip(),
        "build_info": build_info, "config": config, "plan": plan,
        "baseline_harness": baseline_harness,
        "inherited_environment": {key: os.environ.get(key, "default") for key in ENV_KEYS},
        "sha256": {str(filename.resolve()): digest(filename) for filename in sorted(files)},
        "notes": "No timings/builds performed by freeze. Build commands are operator-supplied provenance, not reconstructed from build info. Explicit -pgo=off is required there; build info alone does not expose every flag. External isolation is a separate prerequisite."
    }
    with args.output.open("x") as output:
        json.dump(snapshot, output, indent=2)
        output.write("\n")
    print("Frozen", len(files), "files; no benchmarks run.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

===== .cache/memory-views/frozen-spec.md SHA256 f7431ab031b2234a4480695449192b69d05a2f0628f38b1e1c9a170067b9cba4 =====
# Translation memory views: phase 0

The 2026-10-11 analysis identifies a promising private compiler optimization:
reuse a linear-memory slice header within a short region whose effects cannot
change it. Two sketch result-publication regions reproduce the broad probe's
batch benefit. This is a measured diagnostic, not an implemented hardener pass
or a new public contract. The standalone API and ABI v3 remain unchanged.

Measurements, negative results, conditions, and raw reproduction material are in
[performance.md](performance.md#translation-analysis-positive-phase-0-2026-10-11)
and [the archive](measurements/translation-phase0.txt).

## Demonstrated pattern

Go 1.26.8 inlines wasm2go's checked scalar memory helpers. Their unsafe backing
writes nevertheless invalidate the compiler's knowledge of `Module.memory`:
subsequent accesses reload its pointer and logical length. The current sketch
function, `fn176`, has two terminal result-publication regions where a local
slice view eliminates four such reloads per successful completion. Every guest
load, store, address, integer conversion, bounds check, and stack restoration
remains in place. The logarithm and bin calculation are untouched.

This preserves live backing bytes, rather than making Wasm stack values private.
The `fn84`/`fn176` result addresses cross calls; recognizable stack-pointer
arithmetic alone does not establish nonescape or disjointness. Stores must
remain observable in exported linear memory, including after a later trap.

The diagnostic requires the exact full-module hash and ordinary generated-facade
construction. It does not establish a generic alias or effect analysis. Its
function-number and source-line filters select attribution controls only; they
must not become production selection rules.

## Requirements for the production experiment

Implement recognition in the translation/hardening pipeline, with a conservative
region predicate derived from the demonstrated publication pattern. Define that
predicate before inspecting new holdout results. Regenerate all proof modules
and locks from authored sources; never retain an independently edited module.

The pass must validate the actual bound scalar helper declarations and bodies,
numeric types, receiver, and memory field. Keep existing helper-drift rejection;
leave regions with unproved bindings, effects, or address forms unchanged rather
than rejecting a previously supported module merely because it is ineligible.
Cover helper/import/builtin shadowing and reserved-name collisions explicitly.
For unsafe accesses, prove width-end additions cannot overflow; a spelling match
for `load32` or `uint64` is insufficient. Use logical length, not capacity.

Keep the capture at the first eligible memory access. Preserve operand evaluation
counts and order, integer widths, explicit float rounding, and all guest memory
effects. A local header does not authorize forwarding values, deleting stores,
coalescing accesses, moving bounds checks, or changing math.

Treat unproved direct/indirect calls, imports, bulk operations, memory growth,
header or receiver mutation, pointer/slice escape, and control-flow boundaries
as barriers. Reload after a barrier. Labels, gotos, loops, and joins must not
enter a region after its capture. Predeclare locals where Go's declaration rules
require it; assign the view at region entry rather than hoisting the snapshot.

Establish the memory-ownership precondition explicitly. Generated construction
allocates the Go Module and its byte backing separately, so ordinary guest stores
cannot mutate the Go slice header. Imports can replace the exposed memory header
and must remain barriers. The current experiment does not cover a trusted unsafe
raw-module host fabricating a backing slice that aliases the Module object, or
concurrent raw-module mutation. Do not silently generalize its proof to those
configurations.

## Production experiment specification (2026-10-11)

This private experiment is authorized by the operator's continuation of the
analysis round. It changes no API, ABI, manifest option, ownership rule, or host
contract. Commit this predicate before implementation or new holdout timing.
The following rules select regions structurally; function numbers, source lines,
payload names, and workload results are never selection inputs.

Select a short publication tail inside one lexical Go block:

1. The tail ends in exactly two adjacent validated `store32` calls, followed by
   an assignment restoring a declared receiver `int32` field from a local i32
   plus `i32(nonnegative constant)`. The two stores address the same local i32
   base at offsets zero and four, in either original order.
2. The restoration immediately precedes a goto, a return without effects, or
   the end of the function's outer body. Nested-block fallthrough alone does
   not qualify. This is a structural anchor, not a proof that stack bytes are
   private or that result pointers do not alias.
3. Immediately preceding typed local i32 copies and at most one validated
   `int32(load32(...))` assignment may join the tail, up to four statements.
   No other expression or statement joins it. Require only live-byte accesses;
   do not cache loaded values, combine stores, or infer pointer disjointness.
4. Labels and all other control-flow nodes end the prefix. A direct labelled
   load, store, or copy stays unchanged. A labelled block may contain eligible
   straight-line tails, with each capture inside that block after label entry.
   Capture immediately before the first eligible memory access; never above
   a label or at function entry. No label can target the middle of the resulting
   straight-line region. A later goto successor receives a fresh capture if its
   own tail qualifies. This includes loop re-entry into a labelled block.

Validate binding objects as well as syntax. The bound scalar `load32`, `store32`,
and identity `i32` declarations must match the pinned translator's complete
signatures and bodies. Check their standard `encoding/binary`, `math/bits`,
`unsafe`, and `runtime` imports and architecture constants, plus unshadowed
builtin types and conversions. Resolve receiver/field/local types to the actual
declarations; accept builtin i32 locals, not spelling-equivalent named types.
Scalar drift or unsupported bindings leave the module/region unchanged; existing
bulk-helper drift errors remain errors.

Every eligible load/store's first argument must be exactly the validated memory
field selector on the current bound receiver object. Other buffers, slices,
aliases, fields, receivers, and shadowed receiver names are ineligible. Returns
may be bare or contain only bound local i32 values or integer literals; calls,
field/memory reads, indexing, division/modulo, and other trapping expressions
are ineligible. The restoration follows the view's final use: it is the allowed
tail anchor, not permission to reuse a header after a receiver-field write.
Validate helper compiler directives too: known `go:nosplit` is acceptable;
unexpected binding-affecting directives, including `go:linkname`, are ineligible.

Addresses are exactly `uint32(local_i32)` or
`uint64(uint32(local_i32)) + nonnegative u32 constant`. Preserve the expression
and width as written. The address is at most twice `MaxUint32`, so the helper's
end addition by three cannot overflow uint64. Do not normalize widened offsets
into wrapping i32 arithmetic. Payloads are builtin `uint32(local_i32)` or
`uint32(i32(constant))`. Calls with side-effecting arguments are ineligible.

The Module memory field must be builtin `[]byte`; validate the constructor's
separate `new(Module)` and `make([]byte, ...)` allocations and reject imported
or otherwise unproved memory construction from eligibility. The checked facade
must receive that separately allocated object: merely finding allocation calls
is insufficient. Validate the returned receiver and every generated header
construction path; receiver rebinding or a later unproved unsafe backing alias
makes the module ineligible. Normal owned growth and trusted import-side header
replacement remain allowed only under the following precondition.
The checked facade serializes guest execution. Trusted native hosts must obey
the existing memory ownership precondition: they may replace the header at an
import barrier, but may not fabricate backing storage inside the Go Module
object or race mutation. This pass does not claim to support such fabricated
unsafe aliasing.

Predeclare fresh builtin `[]byte` locals at method entry, assigning each only
at its region entry. Existing name/type collisions leave that method unchanged.
Replace only the original calls' first memory argument; keep all operands,
statement order, guest loads/stores, bounds/traps, and restoration assignments.
Views have method-local lifetime and cannot cross any unproved call, import,
growth, header/receiver write, pointer escape, bulk operation, or control-flow
boundary. Bound validated scalar helper calls are eligible region operations.
No runtime admission, reset, memory, reply, poison, or drain check changes.

Qualification uses freshly built matching before/after harnesses, a freshly
rebuilt independent spike, all broad phase-0 workloads and holdouts, and the
unchanged streaming controls. Run seven interleaved 500 ms samples and seven
reversed one-second samples, isolated with Go 1.26.8, CGO disabled, PGO off.
Preserve every sample; p-values are exploratory and unadjusted. Require repeatable
end-to-end batch benefit without a repeated material guard regression (3% or
more); review smaller detected negatives too. No scalar improvement or M1
acceptance follows from batch throughput. Reject the production pass if proof,
code size, maintenance, or cross-workload effects outweigh the measured benefit;
retain useful independent proofs and complete rejection evidence separately.
The 3% hard rejection threshold does not waive smaller repeated standalone
scalar regressions; the existing standalone guard remains applicable.

## Executable proof and qualification

Add a translated WAT fixture with independent wazero comparisons of returned
values, complete relevant memory, trap categories, and import events. Cover:

- overlapping pointers and partial-width stores, including subsequent reads;
- end-of-memory accesses and wrapping addresses;
- a trap after successful writes, preserving their bytes and observation order;
- calls/imports changing backing bytes;
- growth with spare capacity and growth that reallocates backing storage;
- loops, conditional entry, labels/gotos, and fresh captures after barriers;
- drift and shadowing rejection, plus deliberately broken transforms that the
  executable proofs detect.

Use separate generated Go tests for imports replacing the exposed native slice
header and for logical length below capacity. Arbitrary native header replacement
has no direct Wasm equivalent; WAT/wazero supplies the byte-effect and growth
oracle, while these host-specific cases require direct Go assertions.

Existing generated differential fuzzing is useful but does not cover these
effect histories by itself. Keep per-operation runtime memory checks, reset,
canonical reply validation, immediate poisoning, ownership, and draining Close.
This optimization does not amortize or bypass them.

Freeze freshly generated before/after binaries with identical harnesses and a
fresh independent reference. Repeat all four original workloads, both varied
workloads, negative bins, SQL/large-batch holdouts, and streaming controls. Report
frames, spills, code size, allocations, actual processors, and uncertainty as
well as throughput. Qualify available native architectures and every required
gate; cross compilation alone is not native performance evidence.

The phase 0 gain is limited to the measured original and repeated-value batches.
The broad batch holdout has no detected gain. The broader screen establishes no
scalar speedup; the focused control's small scalar improvement is insufficient
for a standalone latency claim. A production result needs its own qualification.
M1 performance remains unaccepted.

+package harden
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"go/ast"
+	"go/token"
+	"math"
+	"strconv"
+	"strings"
+)
+
+// reusePublicationMemory retains every guest access while reusing its header
+// only in a validated, short publication tail. Unsupported code stays intact.
+func reusePublicationMemory(file *ast.File) {
+	bindings := scalarViewBindings(file)
+	if bindings == nil {
+		return
+	}
+	for _, declaration := range file.Decls {
+		function, ok := declaration.(*ast.FuncDecl)
+		if !ok || function.Body == nil {
+			continue
+		}
+		receiver := bindings.receiver(function)
+		if receiver == nil || !eligibleViewNames(function) {
+			continue
+		}
+		method := bindings.method(function)
+		var names []*ast.Ident
+		ast.Inspect(function.Body, func(node ast.Node) bool {
+			if _, nested := node.(*ast.FuncLit); nested {
+				return false
+			}
+			block, ok := node.(*ast.BlockStmt)
+			if ok {
+				names = method.publicationTails(block, block == function.Body, receiver, names)
+			}
+			return true
+		})
+		if len(names) != 0 {
+			declaration := &ast.DeclStmt{Decl: &ast.GenDecl{Tok: token.VAR, Specs: []ast.Spec{
+				&ast.ValueSpec{Names: names, Type: &ast.ArrayType{Elt: ast.NewIdent("byte")}},
+			}}}
+			function.Body.List = append([]ast.Stmt{declaration}, function.Body.List...)
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func eligibleViewNames(function *ast.FuncDecl) bool {
+	valid := true
+	ast.Inspect(function, func(node ast.Node) bool {
+		if identifier, ok := node.(*ast.Ident); ok &&
+			(strings.HasPrefix(identifier.Name, "cocoonMemoryView") ||
+				identifier.Name == "byte" && viewDeclaration(identifier) != nil) {
+			valid = false
+		}
+		return valid
+	})
+	return valid
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) method(function *ast.FuncDecl) *memoryViewBindings {
+	method := *b
+	method.locals = make(map[any]bool)
+	for _, fields := range []*ast.FieldList{function.Type.Params, function.Type.Results} {
+		if fields != nil {
+			for _, field := range fields.List {
+				method.locals[field] = true
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	ast.Inspect(function.Body, func(node ast.Node) bool {
+		switch node := node.(type) {
+		case *ast.FuncLit:
+			return false
+		case *ast.ValueSpec:
+			method.locals[node] = true
+		case *ast.AssignStmt:
+			if node.Tok == token.DEFINE {
+				method.locals[node] = true
+			}
+		}
+		return true
+	})
+	return &method
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) publicationTails(block *ast.BlockStmt, outer bool, receiver *ast.Ident, names []*ast.Ident) []*ast.Ident {
+	var output []ast.Stmt
+	for index := range len(block.List) {
+		statement := block.List[index]
+		if !b.restoration(statement, receiver) || len(output) < 2 || !b.tailExit(block.List, index, outer) {
+			output = append(output, statement)
+			continue
+		}
+		second, secondBase, secondOffset := b.publicationStore(output[len(output)-1], receiver)
+		first, firstBase, firstOffset := b.publicationStore(output[len(output)-2], receiver)
+		adjacentWords := firstOffset == 0 && secondOffset == 4 || firstOffset == 4 && secondOffset == 0
+		if first == nil || second == nil || !sameViewIdentifier(firstBase, secondBase) || !adjacentWords {
+			output = append(output, statement)
+			continue
+		}
+		start := len(output) - 2
+		loads := 0
+		for count := 0; start > 0 && count < 4; count++ {
+			load, eligible := b.publicationLocal(output[start-1], receiver)
+			if !eligible || load && loads == 1 {
+				break
+			}
+			if load {
+				loads++
+			}
+			start--
+		}
+		// Copies before the first load do not need a header capture.
+		for start < len(output)-2 {
+			load, _ := b.publicationLocal(output[start], receiver)
+			if load {
+				break
+			}
+			start++
+		}
+		name := fmt.Sprintf("cocoonMemoryView%d", len(names)+1)
+		names = append(names, ast.NewIdent(name))
+		capture := &ast.AssignStmt{Tok: token.ASSIGN, Lhs: []ast.Expr{ast.NewIdent(name)}, Rhs: []ast.Expr{
+			&ast.SelectorExpr{X: ast.NewIdent(receiver.Name), Sel: ast.NewIdent("memory")},
+		}}
+		for _, node := range output[start:] {
+			ast.Inspect(node, func(node ast.Node) bool {
+				if call, ok := node.(*ast.CallExpr); ok &&
+					(b.boundCall(call, "load32") || b.boundCall(call, "store32")) {
+					call.Args[0] = ast.NewIdent(name)
+				}
+				return true
+			})
+		}
+		tail := append([]ast.Stmt{capture}, output[start:]...)
+		output = append(output[:start], tail...)
+		output = append(output, statement)
+	}
+	block.List = output
+	return names
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) tailExit(statements []ast.Stmt, index int, outer bool) bool {
+	if index+1 == len(statements) {
+		return outer
+	}
+	switch next := statements[index+1].(type) {
+	case *ast.BranchStmt:
+		return next.Tok == token.GOTO
+	case *ast.ReturnStmt:
+		for _, result := range next.Results {
+			if identifier, ok := result.(*ast.Ident); ok && b.localI32(identifier, 0) {
+				continue
+			}
+			if _, ok := viewInteger(result, -1<<31, 1<<31-1); !ok {
+				return false
+			}
+		}
+		return true
+	default:
+		return false
+	}
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) restoration(statement ast.Stmt, receiver *ast.Ident) bool {
+	assignment, ok := statement.(*ast.AssignStmt)
+	if !ok || assignment.Tok != token.ASSIGN || len(assignment.Lhs) != 1 || len(assignment.Rhs) != 1 {
+		return false
+	}
+	field, ok := assignment.Lhs[0].(*ast.SelectorExpr)
+	if !ok || b.globals[field.Sel.Name] == nil {
+		return false
+	}
+	base, ok := field.X.(*ast.Ident)
+	if !ok || !sameViewIdentifier(base, receiver) {
+		return false
+	}
+	addition, ok := assignment.Rhs[0].(*ast.BinaryExpr)
+	if !ok || addition.Op != token.ADD {
+		return false
+	}
+	local, ok := addition.X.(*ast.Ident)
+	if !ok || !b.localI32(local, 0) {
+		return false
+	}
+	call, ok := addition.Y.(*ast.CallExpr)
+	if !ok || len(call.Args) != 1 || !b.boundCall(call, "i32") {
+		return false
+	}
+	_, ok = viewInteger(call.Args[0], 0, math.MaxInt32)
+	return ok
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) publicationStore(statement ast.Stmt, receiver *ast.Ident) (*ast.CallExpr, *ast.Ident, uint64) {
+	expression, ok := statement.(*ast.ExprStmt)
+	if !ok {
+		return nil, nil, 0
+	}
+	call, ok := expression.X.(*ast.CallExpr)
+	if !ok || len(call.Args) != 3 || !b.boundCall(call, "store32") || !b.memoryArgument(call.Args[0], receiver) ||
+		!b.publicationValue(call.Args[2]) {
+		return nil, nil, 0
+	}
+	base, offset := b.publicationAddress(call.Args[1])
+	if base == nil {
+		return nil, nil, 0
+	}
+	return call, base, offset
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) publicationValue(expression ast.Expr) bool {
+	value, ok := b.conversion(expression, "uint32")
+	if !ok {
+		return false
+	}
+	if identifier, identified := value.(*ast.Ident); identified {
+		return b.localI32(identifier, 0)
+	}
+	call, ok := value.(*ast.CallExpr)
+	if !ok || len(call.Args) != 1 || !b.boundCall(call, "i32") {
+		return false
+	}
+	_, ok = viewInteger(call.Args[0], math.MinInt32, math.MaxInt32)
+	return ok
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) publicationAddress(expression ast.Expr) (base *ast.Ident, offset uint64) {
+	if addition, ok := expression.(*ast.BinaryExpr); ok && addition.Op == token.ADD {
+		constant, ok := viewInteger(addition.Y, 0, math.MaxUint32)
+		if !ok {
+			return nil, 0
+		}
+		offset = uint64(constant) // #nosec G115 -- The nonnegative constant is bounded to MaxUint32.
+		expression = addition.X
+		value, ok := b.conversion(expression, "uint64")
+		if !ok {
+			return nil, 0
+		}
+		expression = value
+	}
+	value, ok := b.conversion(expression, "uint32")
+	if !ok {
+		return nil, 0
+	}
+	base, ok = value.(*ast.Ident)
+	if !ok || !b.localI32(base, 0) {
+		return nil, 0
+	}
+	// Zero extension plus a u32 offset is below 2^33. Keeping the exact
+	// expression preserves wrapping distinctions; the helper's +3 is safe.
+	return base, offset
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) publicationLocal(statement ast.Stmt, receiver *ast.Ident) (load, eligible bool) {
+	assignment, ok := statement.(*ast.AssignStmt)
+	if !ok || (assignment.Tok != token.ASSIGN && assignment.Tok != token.DEFINE) ||
+		len(assignment.Lhs) != 1 || len(assignment.Rhs) != 1 {
+		return false, false
+	}
+	local, ok := assignment.Lhs[0].(*ast.Ident)
+	if !ok || !b.localI32(local, 0) {
+		return false, false
+	}
+	if copied, identified := assignment.Rhs[0].(*ast.Ident); identified {
+		return false, b.localI32(copied, 0)
+	}
+	value, ok := b.conversion(assignment.Rhs[0], "int32")
+	if !ok {
+		return false, false
+	}
+	call, ok := value.(*ast.CallExpr)
+	if !ok || len(call.Args) != 2 || !b.boundCall(call, "load32") || !b.memoryArgument(call.Args[0], receiver) {
+		return false, false
+	}
+	base, _ := b.publicationAddress(call.Args[1])
+	return base != nil, base != nil
+}
+
+func viewInteger(expression ast.Expr, minimum, maximum int64) (int64, bool) {
+	sign := int64(1)
+	if unary, ok := expression.(*ast.UnaryExpr); ok && unary.Op == token.SUB {
+		sign = -1
+		expression = unary.X
+	}
+	literal, ok := expression.(*ast.BasicLit)
+	if !ok || literal.Kind != token.INT {
+		return 0, false
+	}
+	value, err := strconv.ParseInt(literal.Value, 0, 64)
+	if err != nil {
+		return 0, false
+	}
+	value *= sign
+	return value, value >= minimum && value <= maximum
+}

+package harden
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"fmt"
+	"go/ast"
+	"go/format"
+	"go/parser"
+	"go/token"
+	"strconv"
+	"strings"
+)
+
+type memoryViewBindings struct {
+	module    *ast.TypeSpec
+	memory    *ast.Field
+	globals   map[string]*ast.Field
+	functions map[string]*ast.FuncDecl
+	imports   map[string]string
+	declared  map[string]bool
+	locals    map[any]bool
+}
+
+func scalarViewBindings(file *ast.File) *memoryViewBindings {
+	b := &memoryViewBindings{
+		globals: make(map[string]*ast.Field), functions: make(map[string]*ast.FuncDecl),
+		imports:  make(map[string]string),
+		declared: make(map[string]bool),
+	}
+	for _, spec := range file.Imports {
+		path, err := strconv.Unquote(spec.Path.Value)
+		if err != nil || spec.Name != nil {
+			return nil
+		}
+		name := path[strings.LastIndexByte(path, '/')+1:]
+		if b.imports[name] != "" {
+			return nil
+		}
+		b.imports[name] = path
+	}
+	for _, declaration := range file.Decls {
+		if function, ok := declaration.(*ast.FuncDecl); ok && function.Recv == nil {
+			if b.functions[function.Name.Name] != nil {
+				return nil
+			}
+			b.functions[function.Name.Name] = function
+			b.declared[function.Name.Name] = true
+		}
+		if declaration, ok := declaration.(*ast.GenDecl); ok {
+			for _, spec := range declaration.Specs {
+				switch spec := spec.(type) {
+				case *ast.TypeSpec:
+					b.declared[spec.Name.Name] = true
+				case *ast.ValueSpec:
+					for _, name := range spec.Names {
+						b.declared[name.Name] = true
+					}
+				}
+				if spec, ok := spec.(*ast.TypeSpec); ok && spec.Name.Name == "Module" {
+					if b.module != nil {
+						return nil
+					}
+					b.module = spec
+				}
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	if !b.structure() || !b.support(file) || !b.ownedConstruction(file) {
+		return nil
+	}
+	return b
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) structure() bool {
+	if b.module == nil || b.module.Assign.IsValid() || b.module.TypeParams != nil {
+		return false
+	}
+	structure, ok := b.module.Type.(*ast.StructType)
+	if !ok {
+		return false
+	}
+	for _, field := range structure.Fields.List {
+		for _, name := range field.Names {
+			if name.Name == "memory" {
+				if b.memory != nil || !b.byteSlice(field.Type) {
+					return false
+				}
+				b.memory = field
+			}
+			if b.builtin(field.Type, "int32") {
+				b.globals[name.Name] = field
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	return b.memory != nil && len(b.globals) != 0
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) support(file *ast.File) bool {
+	for _, comments := range file.Comments {
+		if !viewDirectives(comments) {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	paths := map[string]string{
+		"binary": "encoding/binary", "bits": "math/bits", "unsafe": "unsafe", "runtime": "runtime", "math": "math",
+	}
+	for name, path := range b.imports {
+		if paths[name] != path {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	for _, name := range []string{"binary", "bits", "unsafe", "runtime"} {
+		if b.imports[name] != paths[name] {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	source := memoryViewSupport
+	for _, width := range []int{16, 32, 64} {
+		source += fmt.Sprintf(memoryViewLoad, width, width/8-1) + fmt.Sprintf(memoryViewStore, width, width/8-1)
+	}
+	expected, err := parser.ParseFile(token.NewFileSet(), "scalar-shapes.go", source, 0)
+	if err != nil {
+		return false
+	}
+	shapes := make(map[string]ast.Node)
+	for _, declaration := range expected.Decls {
+		switch declaration := declaration.(type) {
+		case *ast.FuncDecl:
+			shapes[declaration.Name.Name] = declaration
+		case *ast.GenDecl:
+			for _, spec := range declaration.Specs {
+				if value, ok := spec.(*ast.ValueSpec); ok && len(value.Names) == 1 {
+					shapes[value.Names[0].Name] = value.Values[0]
+				}
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	for _, name := range []string{"load32", "store32", "i32"} {
+		if b.functions[name] == nil {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	for name, function := range b.functions {
+		shape := shapes[name]
+		if shape == nil {
+			continue
+		}
+		if function.Body == nil || !sameViewShape(function.Type, viewFunctionType(shape)) ||
+			!sameViewShape(function.Body, viewFunctionBody(shape)) || !b.supportBindings(function) ||
+			!viewDirectives(function.Doc) {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	for _, name := range []string{"big", "unalignedOK"} {
+		value := viewValueDeclaration(file, name)
+		if value == nil || !sameViewShape(value, shapes[name]) || !b.supportBindings(value) {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return true
+}
+
+func viewFunctionType(node ast.Node) *ast.FuncType {
+	function, ok := node.(*ast.FuncDecl)
+	if !ok {
+		return nil
+	}
+	return function.Type
+}
+
+func viewFunctionBody(node ast.Node) *ast.BlockStmt {
+	function, ok := node.(*ast.FuncDecl)
+	if !ok {
+		return nil
+	}
+	return function.Body
+}
+
+func viewValueDeclaration(file *ast.File, name string) ast.Expr {
+	var result ast.Expr
+	for _, declaration := range file.Decls {
+		group, ok := declaration.(*ast.GenDecl)
+		if !ok || group.Tok != token.CONST {
+			continue
+		}
+		for _, spec := range group.Specs {
+			value, ok := spec.(*ast.ValueSpec)
+			if !ok || len(value.Names) != 1 || len(value.Values) != 1 || value.Type != nil || value.Names[0].Name != name {
+				continue
+			}
+			if result != nil {
+				return nil
+			}
+			result = value.Values[0]
+		}
+	}
+	return result
+}
+
+func sameViewShape(a, b ast.Node) bool {
+	if a == nil || b == nil {
+		return false
+	}
+	var first, second bytes.Buffer
+	return format.Node(&first, token.NewFileSet(), a) == nil &&
+		format.Node(&second, token.NewFileSet(), b) == nil && first.String() == second.String()
+}
+
+func viewDirectives(doc *ast.CommentGroup) bool {
+	if doc == nil {
+		return true
+	}
+	for _, comment := range doc.List {
+		if strings.HasPrefix(comment.Text, "//go:") && comment.Text != "//go:nosplit" {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return true
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) supportBindings(node ast.Node) bool {
+	valid := true
+	ast.Inspect(node, func(node ast.Node) bool {
+		if call, ok := node.(*ast.CallExpr); ok {
+			if name, ok := call.Fun.(*ast.Ident); ok {
+				switch name.Name {
+				case "len", "make", "append", "min":
+					valid = valid && b.builtin(name, name.Name)
+				}
+			}
+		}
+		identifier, ok := node.(*ast.Ident)
+		if !ok {
+			return true
+		}
+		switch identifier.Name {
+		case "int", "int32", "int64", "uint16", "uint32", "uint64", "uintptr", "byte", "false":
+			valid = valid && b.builtin(identifier, identifier.Name)
+		case "binary", "bits", "unsafe", "runtime", "math":
+			valid = valid && viewDeclaration(identifier) == nil && b.imports[identifier.Name] != ""
+		}
+		return valid
+	})
+	return valid
+}
+
+// The selected grammar contains no ambiguous composite-literal keys or type
+// expressions. Parser object references identify declarations in these limited
+// forms; unsupported forms never reach the transform.
+func viewDeclaration(identifier *ast.Ident) any {
+	if identifier.Obj != nil {
+		return identifier.Obj.Decl
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) builtin(expression ast.Expr, name string) bool {
+	identifier, ok := expression.(*ast.Ident)
+	return ok && identifier.Name == name && viewDeclaration(identifier) == nil &&
+		b.imports[name] == "" && !b.declared[name]
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) byteSlice(expression ast.Expr) bool {
+	slice, ok := expression.(*ast.ArrayType)
+	return ok && slice.Len == nil && b.builtin(slice.Elt, "byte")
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) receiver(function *ast.FuncDecl) *ast.Ident {
+	if function.Recv == nil || len(function.Recv.List) != 1 || len(function.Recv.List[0].Names) != 1 {
+		return nil
+	}
+	pointer, ok := function.Recv.List[0].Type.(*ast.StarExpr)
+	if !ok {
+		return nil
+	}
+	name, ok := pointer.X.(*ast.Ident)
+	if !ok || viewDeclaration(name) != b.module {
+		return nil
+	}
+	return function.Recv.List[0].Names[0]
+}
+
+func sameViewIdentifier(a, c *ast.Ident) bool {
+	return a != nil && c != nil && viewDeclaration(a) != nil && viewDeclaration(a) == viewDeclaration(c) && a.Name == c.Name
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) memoryArgument(expression ast.Expr, receiver *ast.Ident) bool {
+	field, ok := expression.(*ast.SelectorExpr)
+	if !ok || field.Sel.Name != "memory" {
+		return false
+	}
+	base, ok := field.X.(*ast.Ident)
+	return ok && sameViewIdentifier(base, receiver)
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) boundCall(call *ast.CallExpr, name string) bool {
+	identifier, ok := call.Fun.(*ast.Ident)
+	return ok && identifier.Name == name && b.functions[name] != nil &&
+		viewDeclaration(identifier) == b.functions[name] && !call.Ellipsis.IsValid()
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) conversion(expression ast.Expr, name string) (ast.Expr, bool) {
+	call, ok := expression.(*ast.CallExpr)
+	if !ok || len(call.Args) != 1 || call.Ellipsis.IsValid() || !b.builtin(call.Fun, name) {
+		return nil, false
+	}
+	return call.Args[0], true
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) localI32(identifier *ast.Ident, depth int) bool {
+	if identifier == nil || depth > 16 || identifier.Name == "_" {
+		return false
+	}
+	if !b.locals[viewDeclaration(identifier)] {
+		return false
+	}
+	switch declaration := viewDeclaration(identifier).(type) {
+	case *ast.Field:
+		return b.builtin(declaration.Type, "int32")
+	case *ast.ValueSpec:
+		return b.builtin(declaration.Type, "int32")
+	case *ast.AssignStmt:
+		if declaration.Tok != token.DEFINE || len(declaration.Lhs) != len(declaration.Rhs) {
+			return false
+		}
+		for i, expression := range declaration.Lhs {
+			name, ok := expression.(*ast.Ident)
+			if ok && name.Name == identifier.Name {
+				if _, converted := b.conversion(declaration.Rhs[i], "int32"); converted {
+					return true
+				}
+				if name, ok := declaration.Rhs[i].(*ast.Ident); ok {
+					return b.localI32(name, depth+1)
+				}
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}

+package harden
+
+import (
+	"go/ast"
+	"go/token"
+)
+
+// The translator owns its backing allocation. Native Init/Memory adapters may
+// replace it only under the existing trusted, nonconcurrent host precondition.
+// Generated code cannot rebind the receiver or install an unproved header.
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) ownedConstruction(file *ast.File) bool {
+	constructor := b.functions["New"]
+	if constructor == nil || constructor.Body == nil || constructor.Type.TypeParams != nil ||
+		constructor.Type.Results == nil || len(constructor.Type.Results.List) != 1 ||
+		len(constructor.Type.Results.List[0].Names) != 0 ||
+		!b.modulePointer(constructor.Type.Results.List[0].Type) || len(constructor.Body.List) < 3 {
+		return false
+	}
+	allocation, ok := constructor.Body.List[0].(*ast.AssignStmt)
+	if !ok || allocation.Tok != token.DEFINE || len(allocation.Lhs) != 1 || len(allocation.Rhs) != 1 {
+		return false
+	}
+	owner, ok := allocation.Lhs[0].(*ast.Ident)
+	if !ok {
+		return false
+	}
+	call, ok := allocation.Rhs[0].(*ast.CallExpr)
+	if !ok || !b.builtin(call.Fun, "new") || call.Ellipsis.IsValid() || len(call.Args) != 1 {
+		return false
+	}
+	module, ok := call.Args[0].(*ast.Ident)
+	if !ok || viewDeclaration(module) != b.module {
+		return false
+	}
+	final, ok := constructor.Body.List[len(constructor.Body.List)-1].(*ast.ReturnStmt)
+	if !ok || len(final.Results) != 1 {
+		return false
+	}
+	returned, ok := final.Results[0].(*ast.Ident)
+	if !ok || !sameViewIdentifier(returned, owner) {
+		return false
+	}
+	allocations := 0
+	valid := true
+	for _, declaration := range file.Decls {
+		function, ok := declaration.(*ast.FuncDecl)
+		if !ok {
+			ast.Inspect(declaration, func(node ast.Node) bool {
+				if _, literal := node.(*ast.FuncLit); literal {
+					valid = false
+				}
+				if selector, ok := node.(*ast.SelectorExpr); ok {
+					if name, ok := selector.X.(*ast.Ident); ok && name.Name == "unsafe" {
+						valid = false
+					}
+				}
+				return valid
+			})
+			if !valid {
+				return false
+			}
+			continue
+		}
+		if function.Body == nil {
+			continue
+		}
+		// These complete bodies were validated by support. Their indirect byte
+		// stores and owned growth are the only proved pointer-write operations.
+		if function.Recv == nil && (viewScalarHelper(function.Name.Name) || function.Name.Name == "memory_grow") {
+			continue
+		}
+		receiver := b.receiver(function)
+		if function == constructor {
+			receiver = owner
+		}
+		ast.Inspect(function.Body, func(node ast.Node) bool {
+			if !valid {
+				return false
+			}
+			switch node := node.(type) {
+			case *ast.DeferStmt:
+				valid = valid && function != constructor
+			case *ast.RangeStmt:
+				if node.Tok == token.ASSIGN {
+					valid = valid && !viewReceiverTarget(node.Key, receiver) && !viewReceiverTarget(node.Value, receiver) &&
+						!viewMemoryField(node.Key) && !viewMemoryField(node.Value)
+				}
+			case *ast.SelectorExpr:
+				if name, ok := node.X.(*ast.Ident); ok && name.Name == "unsafe" {
+					// Full scalar helper bodies are validated above. No other
+					// translated function may fabricate a native backing alias.
+					valid = valid && function.Recv == nil && viewScalarHelper(function.Name.Name)
+				}
+			case *ast.AssignStmt:
+				for i, target := range node.Lhs {
+					target = viewUnwrap(target)
+					if node != allocation && viewReceiverTarget(target, receiver) {
+						valid = false
+					}
+					if b.memoryArgument(target, receiver) {
+						valid = valid && function == constructor && node.Tok == token.ASSIGN &&
+							len(node.Lhs) == 1 && len(node.Rhs) == 1 && b.ownedMemory(node.Rhs[i])
+						allocations++
+					}
+					if field, ok := target.(*ast.SelectorExpr); ok && field.Sel.Name == "memory" &&
+						!b.memoryArgument(target, receiver) {
+						valid = false
+					}
+				}
+			case *ast.ReturnStmt:
+				if function == constructor && node != final {
+					valid = false
+				}
+			case *ast.UnaryExpr:
+				addressed := viewUnwrap(node.X)
+				if name, ok := addressed.(*ast.Ident); ok && node.Op == token.AND && sameViewIdentifier(name, receiver) {
+					valid = false
+				}
+				if node.Op == token.AND && viewMemoryField(addressed) {
+					valid = valid && b.memoryArgument(addressed, receiver) && b.provenMemoryAddress(function, node)
+				}
+			}
+			return valid
+		})
+		if !valid {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return valid && allocations == 1
+}
+
+func viewReceiverTarget(expression ast.Expr, receiver *ast.Ident) bool {
+	expression = viewUnwrap(expression)
+	if name, ok := expression.(*ast.Ident); ok {
+		return sameViewIdentifier(name, receiver)
+	}
+	_, indirect := expression.(*ast.StarExpr)
+	return indirect
+}
+
+func viewUnwrap(expression ast.Expr) ast.Expr {
+	for {
+		parenthesized, ok := expression.(*ast.ParenExpr)
+		if !ok {
+			return expression
+		}
+		expression = parenthesized.X
+	}
+}
+
+func viewMemoryField(expression ast.Expr) bool {
+	field, ok := viewUnwrap(expression).(*ast.SelectorExpr)
+	return ok && field.Sel.Name == "memory"
+}
+
+func viewScalarHelper(name string) bool {
+	switch name {
+	case "load16", "store16", "load32", "store32", "load64", "store64":
+		return true
+	default:
+		return false
+	}
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) modulePointer(expression ast.Expr) bool {
+	pointer, ok := expression.(*ast.StarExpr)
+	if !ok {
+		return false
+	}
+	name, ok := pointer.X.(*ast.Ident)
+	return ok && viewDeclaration(name) == b.module
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) ownedMemory(expression ast.Expr) bool {
+	call, ok := expression.(*ast.CallExpr)
+	return ok && b.builtin(call.Fun, "make") && !call.Ellipsis.IsValid() &&
+		(len(call.Args) == 2 || len(call.Args) == 3) && b.byteSlice(call.Args[0])
+}
+
+func (b *memoryViewBindings) provenMemoryAddress(function *ast.FuncDecl, address *ast.UnaryExpr) bool {
+	proven := false
+	ast.Inspect(function.Body, func(node ast.Node) bool {
+		call, ok := node.(*ast.CallExpr)
+		if ok && len(call.Args) == 3 && call.Args[0] == address && b.boundCall(call, "memory_grow") {
+			proven = true
+		}
+		return true
+	})
+	if proven {
+		return true
+	}
+	// The canonical exported adapter hands the header to the trusted host. It
+	// does not create backing storage or a snapshot usable by this pass.
+	if function.Name.Name != "Xmemory" || len(function.Body.List) != 1 {
+		return false
+	}
+	statement, ok := function.Body.List[0].(*ast.ReturnStmt)
+	if !ok || len(statement.Results) != 1 {
+		return false
+	}
+	call, ok := statement.Results[0].(*ast.CallExpr)
+	if !ok || len(call.Args) != 1 || call.Args[0] != address {
+		return false
+	}
+	conversion, ok := call.Fun.(*ast.ParenExpr)
+	if !ok {
+		return false
+	}
+	pointer, ok := conversion.X.(*ast.StarExpr)
+	if !ok {
+		return false
+	}
+	name, ok := pointer.X.(*ast.Ident)
+	if !ok || name.Name != "wasmMemory" {
+		return false
+	}
+	typeSpec, ok := viewDeclaration(name).(*ast.TypeSpec)
+	return ok && !typeSpec.Assign.IsValid() && typeSpec.TypeParams == nil && b.byteSlice(typeSpec.Type)
+}

+package harden
+
+// These shapes describe translator support code, not a payload implementation.
+// Eligibility is optional: any drift leaves the scalar-view pass inactive.
+const memoryViewSupport = `package wasm
+const big = false ||
+ runtime.GOARCH == "ppc64" || runtime.GOARCH == "s390x" ||
+ runtime.GOARCH == "mips" || runtime.GOARCH == "mips64"
+const unalignedOK = false ||
+ runtime.GOARCH == "386" || runtime.GOARCH == "amd64" ||
+ runtime.GOARCH == "arm64" || runtime.GOARCH == "loong64" ||
+ runtime.GOARCH == "ppc64" || runtime.GOARCH == "ppc64le" ||
+ runtime.GOARCH == "s390x" || runtime.GOARCH == "wasm"
+func i32(x int32) int32 { return x }
+func memory_grow(mem *[]byte, delta, max int64) int64 {
+ buf := *mem
+ len := len(buf)
+ old := len >> 16
+ if delta == 0 { return int64(old) }
+ max = int64(min(uint64(max), math.MaxInt>>16))
+ new, c := bits.Add64(uint64(old), uint64(delta), 0)
+ if c != 0 || new > uint64(max) { return -1 }
+ *mem = append(buf, make([]byte, int(new<<16)-len)...)
+ return int64(old)
+}
+`
+
+const memoryViewLoad = `
+func load%[1]d[T uint32 | uint64](mem []byte, addr T) uint%[1]d {
+ if !unalignedOK { return binary.LittleEndian.Uint%[1]d(mem[addr:]) }
+ _ = mem[uint64(addr)+%[2]d]
+ val := *(*uint%[1]d)(unsafe.Add(unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(mem)), uintptr(addr)))
+ if big { return bits.ReverseBytes%[1]d(val) }
+ return val
+}
+`
+
+const memoryViewStore = `
+func store%[1]d[T uint32 | uint64](mem []byte, addr T, val uint%[1]d) {
+ if !unalignedOK { binary.LittleEndian.PutUint%[1]d(mem[addr:], val); return }
+ if big { val = bits.ReverseBytes%[1]d(val) }
+ _ = mem[uint64(addr)+%[2]d]
+ *(*uint%[1]d)(unsafe.Add(unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(mem)), uintptr(addr))) = val
+}
+`

+const publication = `
+func (receiver *Module) publish(base, value, stack int32) {
+ store32(receiver.memory, uint32(base), uint32(value))
+ store32(receiver.memory, uint64(uint32(base))+4, uint32(i32(7)))
+ receiver.g0 = stack + i32(16)
+}
+`

+// The trap fixture has only a load32. Include the pinned translator's store32
+// shape here; the executable WAT proof obtains both helpers from wasm2go.
+const publicationStore = `
+//go:nosplit
+func store32[T uint32 | uint64](mem []byte, addr T, val uint32) {
+ if !unalignedOK { binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(mem[addr:], val); return }
+ if big { val = bits.ReverseBytes32(val) }
+ _ = mem[uint64(addr)+3]
+ *(*uint32)(unsafe.Add(unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(mem)), uintptr(addr))) = val
+}
+`

+func viewFixture(t *testing.T, method string) []byte {
+	t.Helper()
+	source, err := os.ReadFile("../../rt/internal/trapfix/testdata/raw.go.txt")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	source = bytes.Replace(source, []byte("type Module struct {"), []byte("type Module struct {\n g0 int32"), 1)
+	return append(source, []byte(publicationStore+method)...)
+}
+
+func rewriteViewFixture(t *testing.T, source []byte) []byte {
+	t.Helper()
+	names, err := harden.Required(source)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	output, err := harden.Rewrite(source, names)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	return output
+}
+
+func TestPublicationMemoryViews(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+	for _, method := range []string{
+		publication,
+		strings.ReplaceAll(publication, "publish", "differentPayload"),
+	} {
+		output := rewriteViewFixture(t, viewFixture(t, method))
+		if bytes.Count(output, []byte("cocoonMemoryView1 = receiver.memory")) != 1 ||
+			bytes.Count(output, []byte("store32(cocoonMemoryView1,")) != 2 ||
+			!bytes.Contains(output, []byte("var cocoonMemoryView1 []byte")) {
+			t.Fatal("structural publication tail was not rewritten")
+		}
+	}
+	source := bytes.ReplaceAll(viewFixture(t, publication), []byte("g0"), []byte("anotherGlobal"))
+	if !bytes.Contains(rewriteViewFixture(t, source), []byte("store32(cocoonMemoryView1,")) {
+		t.Fatal("global name affected eligibility")
+	}
+}

+func TestPublicationEntryAndLiveLoad(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+	method := `
+func (m *Module) publish(base, value, stack int32) {
+ if value == 0 { goto join }
+ store32(m.memory, uint64(uint32(base))+4, uint32(value))
+ store32(m.memory, uint32(base), uint32(i32(9)))
+ m.g0 = stack + i32(16)
+ goto join
+join:
+ value = int32(load32(m.memory, uint32(base)))
+ loaded := int32(load32(m.memory, uint64(uint32(base))+4))
+ copied := loaded
+ store32(m.memory, uint32(base), uint32(copied))
+ store32(m.memory, uint64(uint32(base))+4, uint32(value))
+ m.g0 = stack + i32(16)
+}
+`
+	output := rewriteViewFixture(t, viewFixture(t, method))
+	if bytes.Count(output, []byte("= m.memory")) != 2 ||
+		!bytes.Contains(output, []byte("join:\n\tvalue = int32(load32(m.memory,")) ||
+		!bytes.Contains(output, []byte("load32(cocoonMemoryView2,")) ||
+		bytes.Count(output, []byte("store32(cocoonMemoryView")) != 4 {
+		t.Fatal("label entry or live-memory access changed", string(output[len(output)-1500:]))
+	}
+}

+func TestPublicationUnsupportedShapesStayUnchanged(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+	for _, change := range [][2]string{
+		{"uint64(uint32(base))+4", "uint64(uint32(base))+8"},
+		{"uint64(uint32(base))+4", "uint32(base+i32(4))"},
+		{"uint64(uint32(base))+4", "uint64(base)+4"},
+		{"uint64(uint32(base))+4", "uint64(uint32(base))+0xffffffffffffffff"},
+		{"receiver.g0 = stack + i32(16)", "receiver.g0 = stack"},
+		{"uint32(value)", "uint32(value+i32(1))"},
+		{"uint32(value)", "uint32(load32(receiver.memory, uint32(base)))"},
+		{"store32(receiver.memory, uint64", "receiver.fn0()\n store32(receiver.memory, uint64"},
+		{"store32(receiver.memory, uint64", "between:\n store32(receiver.memory, uint64"},
+		{"receiver.g0 = stack + i32(16)", "receiver.g0 = stack + i32(16)\n return int32(load32(receiver.memory, uint32(base)))"},
+		{"receiver.g0 = stack + i32(16)", "receiver.g0 = stack + i32(16)\n receiver.fn0()"},
+		{"base, value, stack int32", "base int64, value, stack int32"},
+		{"base, value, stack int32", "base, value, stack int32, byte int32"},
+		{"base, value, stack int32", "base, value, stack int32, cocoonMemoryView1 int32"},
+	} {
+		source := viewFixture(t, strings.Replace(publication, change[0], change[1], 1))
+		if bytes.Contains(rewriteViewFixture(t, source), []byte("var cocoonMemoryView")) {
+			t.Fatalf("unproved publication shape rewritten: %q", change[1])
+		}
+	}
+}

+func TestPublicationHelperAndOwnershipDrift(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+	for _, change := range [][2]string{
+		{"_ = mem[uint64(addr)+3]", "_ = mem[uint64(addr)+2]"},
+		{"func i32(x int32) int32 { return x }", "func i32(x int32) int32 { return x + 1 }"},
+		{"runtime.GOARCH == \"ppc64\"", "runtime.GOARCH == \"other\""},
+		{"\"encoding/binary\"", "\"example.com/binary\""},
+		{"\"unsafe\"", "native \"unsafe\""},
+		{"m.memory = make([]byte, 65536)", "m.memory = make([]byte, 65536)\n m.memory = unsafe.Slice((*byte)(unsafe.Pointer(m)),65536)"},
+		{"return m\n}", "m = new(Module)\n return m\n}"},
+		{"return m\n}", "return new(Module)\n}"},
+		{"return m\n}", "p := &m\n *p = new(Module)\n return m\n}"},
+		{"return m\n}", "*(&m) = new(Module)\n return m\n}"},
+		{"return m\n}", "p := m\n *p = Module{}\n return m\n}"},
+		{"return m\n}", "for _, m = range []*Module{new(Module)} {}\n return m\n}"},
+		{"func New() *Module {", "func New() (result *Module) {"},
+		{"return m\n}", "defer func() { m.memory = nil }()\n return m\n}"},
+		{"return m\n}", "((m)) = new(Module)\n return m\n}"},
+		{"return m\n}", "p := m\n (*p) = Module{}\n return m\n}"},
+		{"return m\n}", "(m.memory) = nil\n return m\n}"},
+		{"return m\n}", "p := &(m)\n (*p) = new(Module)\n return m\n}"},
+		{"return m\n}", "p := &(m.memory)\n (*p) = nil\n return m\n}"},
+		{"return m\n}", "for _, (m) = range []*Module{new(Module)} {}\n return m\n}"},
+		{"return m\n}", "for _, m.memory = range [][]byte{nil} {}\n return m\n}"},
+		{"return m\n}", "for _, (m.memory) = range [][]byte{nil} {}\n return m\n}"},
+		{"func New() *Module {", "var clearModule = func(p *Module) { *p = Module{} }\n func New() *Module {"},
+		{"func New() *Module {", "type int int64\n func New() *Module {"},
+		{"//go:nosplit\nfunc load32", "//go:linkname load32 other\nfunc load32"},
+		{"base, value, stack int32", "base, value, stack int32, uint32 func(int32) uint32"},
+		{"base, value, stack int32", "base, value, stack int32, store32 func([]byte,uint32,uint32)"},
+		{"base, value, stack int32", "base, value, stack int32, other []byte"},
+	} {
+		source := viewFixture(t, publication)
+		if !bytes.Contains(source, []byte(change[0])) {
+			t.Fatalf("missing drift target %q", change[0])
+		}
+		source = bytes.Replace(source, []byte(change[0]), []byte(change[1]), 1)
+		if strings.Contains(change[1], "other []byte") {
+			source = bytes.ReplaceAll(source, []byte("store32(receiver.memory"), []byte("store32(other"))
+		}
+		if bytes.Contains(rewriteViewFixture(t, source), []byte("var cocoonMemoryView")) {
+			t.Fatalf("unproved binding/construction rewritten: %q", change[1])
+		}
+	}
+}

+func TestPublicationShadowedBindings(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+	// The first store's explicit widened zero offset keeps these fake helper
+	// signatures valid Go while retaining the same structural offset pair.
+	stores := `
+ store32(receiver.memory, uint64(uint32(base))+0, uint32(value))
+ store32(receiver.memory, uint64(uint32(base))+4, uint32(i32(7)))
+ receiver.g0 = stack + i32(16)
+ return
+`
+	fakeStore := `func(memory []byte, address uint64, value uint32) {}`
+	for _, scope := range []string{
+		"store32 := " + fakeStore + stores,
+		"if store32 := " + fakeStore + "; value != 0 {" + stores + "}",
+		"for _, store32 := range []func([]byte, uint64, uint32){" + fakeStore + "} {" + stores + "}",
+		"switch store32 := " + fakeStore + "; value { case 1:" + stores + "}",
+		"{ uint32 := func(value int32) uint32 { return 0 };" + stores + "}",
+		"{ uint64 := func(value uint32) uint64 { return 0 };" + stores + "}",
+		"{ i32 := func(value int32) int32 { return 0 };" + stores + "}",
+		"{ receiver := new(Module);" + stores + "}",
+		"{ type word int32; var base word;" + stores + "}",
+	} {
+		method := "func (receiver *Module) publish(base, value, stack int32) {\n" + scope + "\n}"
+		if bytes.Contains(rewriteViewFixture(t, viewFixture(t, method)), []byte("var cocoonMemoryView")) {
+			t.Fatalf("shadowed declaration transformed: %s", scope)
+		}
+	}
+}

+// TestMemoryViewSemantics executes the actual translated/hardened module. The
+// CGO-disabled Go child is not race-instrumented by a race-enabled parent.
+func TestMemoryViewSemantics(t *testing.T) {
+	if os.Getenv("COCOON_SMOKE") != "1" {
+		t.Skip("set COCOON_SMOKE=1 with the pinned Binaryen and wasm2go tools installed")
+	}
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(t.Context(), 3*time.Minute)
+	defer cancel()
+	root, err := filepath.Abs("../..")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	goExecutable, err := exec.LookPath("go")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	work := t.TempDir()
+	runner := memoryViewRunner(work)
+	memoryViewTools(ctx, t, runner, root, goExecutable)
+	raw, optimized := filepath.Join(work, "raw.wasm"), filepath.Join(work, "module.wasm")
+	arguments := append([]string{filepath.Join(root, "internal", "smoke", "testdata", "memory-views.wat"), "-o", raw}, build.Features()...)
+	runNumeric(ctx, t, runner, root, "wasm-as", arguments...)
+	arguments = append([]string{raw, "-O3", "-o", optimized}, build.Features()...)
+	runNumeric(ctx, t, runner, root, "wasm-opt", arguments...)
+	translatedPath := filepath.Join(work, "module.go")
+	runNumeric(ctx, t, runner, root, goExecutable, "tool", "wasm2go", "-unsafe", "-pkg", "wasm", "-o", translatedPath, optimized)
+	translated := read(t, translatedPath)
+	required, err := harden.Required(translated)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	hardened, err := harden.Rewrite(translated, required)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	assertMemoryViewRegions(t, hardened)
+	histories := memoryViewGoldens(ctx, t, read(t, optimized))
+	encoded, err := json.Marshal(histories)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	write(t, translatedPath, string(hardened))
+	write(t, filepath.Join(work, "go.mod"), "module example.com/memory-view-fixture\n\ngo 1.26.0\n")
+	write(t, filepath.Join(work, "module_test.go"), memoryViewModuleTests)
+	write(t, filepath.Join(work, "histories.json"), string(encoded))
+	runNumeric(ctx, t, runner, work, goExecutable, "test", "-pgo=off", "-count=1", "-timeout=45s", "./...")
+	checkMemoryViewMutants(ctx, t, runner, work, goExecutable, translatedPath, hardened)
+}

+func memoryViewRunner(work string) build.ExecRunner {
+	environment := []string{"CGO_ENABLED=0", "GOWORK=off", "GOTOOLCHAIN=local", "GOENV=off", "GOPROXY=off", "GOSUMDB=off", "GOVCS=*:off", "GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false"}
+	if os.Getenv("GOCACHE") == "" {
+		environment = append(environment, "GOCACHE="+filepath.Join(work, "go-cache"))
+	}
+	return build.ExecRunner{Environment: environment}
+}

+func memoryViewTools(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, runner build.ExecRunner, root, goExecutable string) {
+	t.Helper()
+	for _, program := range []string{"wasm-as", "wasm-opt"} {
+		version := strings.Fields(string(runNumeric(ctx, t, runner, root, program, "--version")))
+		if len(version) < 3 || version[0] != program || version[1] != "version" || version[2] != manifest.BinaryenVersion {
+			t.Fatalf("%s requires version %s, got %v", program, manifest.BinaryenVersion, version)
+		}
+	}
+	version := strings.Fields(string(runNumeric(ctx, t, runner, root, goExecutable, "tool", "wasm2go", "-version")))
+	if len(version) != 2 || version[0] != "wasm2go" || version[1] != manifest.Wasm2GoVersion {
+		t.Fatalf("wasm2go requires %s, got %v", manifest.Wasm2GoVersion, version)
+	}
+}

+func memoryViewCases() []viewHistory {
+	step := func(name string, args ...uint32) viewStep { return viewStep{Export: name, Args: args} }
+	return []viewHistory{
+		{Name: "aliases", Steps: []viewStep{
+			step("publish", 32, 0x11223344, 0x55667788),
+			step("copy_tuple", 32, 32, 0xaabbccdd),
+			step("copy_tuple", 34, 36, 0x01234567),
+			step("reverse", 33, 0x10203040, 0x50607080),
+			step("mixed_tuple", 35, 33),
+		}},
+		{Name: "exact-end", Steps: []viewStep{step("publish", 65528, 0x11223344, 0x55667788)}},
+		{Name: "trap-prefix", Steps: []viewStep{step("publish", 65532, 0x11223344, 0x55667788)}},
+		{Name: "reverse-trap", Steps: []viewStep{step("reverse", 65532, 0x11223344, 0x55667788)}},
+		{Name: "source-trap", Steps: []viewStep{step("copy_tuple", 0, 65534, 0x55667788)}},
+		{Name: "partial-trap", Steps: []viewStep{step("mixed_tuple", 0, 65535)}},
+		{Name: "negative-base", Steps: []viewStep{step("publish", 0xffffffff, 0x11223344, 0x55667788)}},
+		{Name: "widened-base", Steps: []viewStep{step("reverse", 0xfffffffc, 0x11223344, 0x55667788)}},
+		{Name: "wrapping-trap", Steps: []viewStep{step("wrapping_tuple", 0xfffffffc)}},
+		{Name: "imports-and-growth", Steps: []viewStep{
+			step("after_import", 1, 64), step("after_import", 2, 65536),
+			step("grow_tuple", 131072, 1), step("grow_tuple", 80, 0), step("grow_tuple", 88, 8),
+		}},
+		{Name: "loop-growth", Steps: []viewStep{step("loop_tuples", 2, 65536, 2)}},
+		{Name: "loop-observation", Steps: []viewStep{step("loop_tuples", 1, 0, 3)}},
+		{Name: "zero-loop", Steps: []viewStep{step("loop_tuples", 2, 65536, 0)}},
+		{Name: "conditional-entry", Steps: []viewStep{step("conditional_tuple", 0, 80), step("conditional_tuple", 1, 80)}},
+	}
+}

+func memoryViewGoldens(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, wasm []byte) []viewHistory {
+	t.Helper()
+	runtime := wazero.NewRuntimeWithConfig(ctx, wazero.NewRuntimeConfigInterpreter())
+	t.Cleanup(func() {
+		if err := runtime.Close(context.WithoutCancel(ctx)); err != nil {
+			t.Error(err)
+		}
+	})
+	var events []viewEvent
+	_, err := runtime.NewHostModuleBuilder("env").NewFunctionBuilder().WithFunc(func(_ context.Context, module api.Module, kind uint32) {
+		before, ok := module.Memory().ReadUint32Le(0)
+		if !ok {
+			t.Fatal("fixture import cannot observe memory")
+		}
+		events = append(events, viewEvent{Kind: kind, Before: before, Pages: module.Memory().Size() >> 16})
+		if kind == 0 {
+			return
+		}
+		if kind == 2 {
+			if _, grown := module.Memory().Grow(1); !grown {
+				t.Fatal("fixture import growth failed")
+			}
+		}
+		count := len(events)
+		if count > 1024 {
+			t.Fatal("fixture import history exceeded its bound")
+		}
+		number := uint32(count) // #nosec G115 -- len(events) is nonnegative and bounded to 1024 above.
+		if kind > 2 || !module.Memory().WriteUint32Le(32, 0x0a0b0c0d+number) {
+			t.Fatal("unsupported fixture import", kind)
+		}
+	}).Export("touch").Instantiate(ctx)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	compiled, err := runtime.CompileModule(ctx, wasm)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	histories := memoryViewCases()
+	for index := range histories {
+		events = nil
+		module, instantiateErr := runtime.InstantiateModule(ctx, compiled, wazero.NewModuleConfig().WithName(histories[index].Name))
+		if instantiateErr != nil {
+			t.Fatal(instantiateErr)
+		}
+		for step := range histories[index].Steps {
+			memoryViewGoldenStep(ctx, t, module, &histories[index].Steps[step])
+			// Imports append to events during the operation, so snapshot afterward.
+			histories[index].Steps[step].Events = append([]viewEvent(nil), events...)
+		}
+		assertMemoryViewOracle(t, histories[index])
+		if closeErr := module.Close(ctx); closeErr != nil {
+			t.Fatal(closeErr)
+		}
+	}
+	return histories
+}
+
+func memoryViewGoldenStep(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, module api.Module, step *viewStep) {
+	t.Helper()
+	args := make([]uint64, len(step.Args))
+	for index, value := range step.Args {
+		args[index] = uint64(value)
+	}
+	function := module.ExportedFunction(step.Export)
+	if function == nil {
+		t.Fatal("missing fixture export", step.Export)
+	}
+	result, err := function.Call(ctx, args...)
+	if err != nil {
+		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "out of bounds memory access") {
+			t.Fatal("unexpected fixture trap", err)
+		}
+		step.Trap = "memory"
+	} else if len(result) != 0 {
+		t.Fatal("unexpected fixture results", result)
+	}
+	memory, ok := module.Memory().Read(0, module.Memory().Size())
+	if !ok {
+		t.Fatal("fixture memory snapshot failed")
+	}
+	step.Memory = bytes.Clone(memory)
+	stack, stackErr := module.ExportedFunction("stack_value").Call(ctx)
+	if stackErr != nil || len(stack) != 1 {
+		t.Fatal(stack, stackErr)
+	}
+	step.Stack = uint32(stack[0]) // #nosec G115 -- The validated export returns Wasm i32 bits.
+}
+
+func assertMemoryViewOracle(t *testing.T, history viewHistory) {
+	t.Helper()
+	step := history.Steps[0]
+	switch history.Name {
+	case "trap-prefix":
+		if step.Trap != "memory" || binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(step.Memory[65532:]) != 0x11223344 || step.Stack != 49136 {
+			t.Fatal("original Wasm did not preserve the first store before its trap")
+		}
+	case "reverse-trap":
+		if step.Trap != "memory" || binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(step.Memory[65532:]) != 0 || step.Stack != 49136 {
+			t.Fatal("original Wasm reordered the reverse-store trap")
+		}
+	case "wrapping-trap":
+		if step.Trap != "memory" || binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(step.Memory) != 0x55667788 || step.Stack != 49136 {
+			t.Fatal("original Wasm conflated widened and wrapping addresses")
+		}
+	case "widened-base":
+		if step.Trap != "memory" || binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(step.Memory) != 0 || step.Stack != 49136 {
+			t.Fatal("original Wasm truncated a widened address above MaxUint32")
+		}
+	case "partial-trap":
+		if step.Trap != "memory" || step.Memory[65535] != 0xab || step.Stack != 49136 {
+			t.Fatal("original Wasm lost its partial-width trap prefix")
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func assertMemoryViewRegions(t *testing.T, source []byte) {
+	t.Helper()
+	file, err := parser.ParseFile(token.NewFileSet(), "module.go", source, 0)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	wanted := map[string]bool{"Xpublish": true, "Xreverse": true, "Xcopy_tuple": true, "Xmixed_tuple": true, "Xafter_import": true, "Xgrow_tuple": true, "Xloop_tuples": true, "Xconditional_tuple": true}
+	for _, declaration := range file.Decls {
+		function, ok := declaration.(*ast.FuncDecl)
+		if !ok {
+			continue
+		}
+		if function.Name.Name == "Xwrapping_tuple" {
+			ast.Inspect(function.Body, func(node ast.Node) bool {
+				if identifier, named := node.(*ast.Ident); named && strings.HasPrefix(identifier.Name, "cocoonMemoryView") {
+					t.Fatal("wrapping address shape must remain ineligible")
+				}
+				return true
+			})
+		}
+		if !wanted[function.Name.Name] {
+			continue
+		}
+		stores := 0
+		ast.Inspect(function.Body, func(node ast.Node) bool {
+			call, called := node.(*ast.CallExpr)
+			if called && len(call.Args) == 3 {
+				name, named := call.Fun.(*ast.Ident)
+				view, viewed := call.Args[0].(*ast.Ident)
+				if named && name.Name == "store32" && viewed && strings.HasPrefix(view.Name, "cocoonMemoryView") {
+					stores++
+				}
+			}
+			return true
+		})
+		if stores != 2 {
+			t.Fatalf("fixture method %s must execute two rewritten publication stores, got %d", function.Name.Name, stores)
+		}
+		delete(wanted, function.Name.Name)
+	}
+	if len(wanted) != 0 {
+		t.Fatal("missing rewritten fixture methods", wanted)
+	}
+}
+
+func checkMemoryViewMutants(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, runner build.ExecRunner, work, goExecutable, path string, source []byte) {
+	t.Helper()
+	for _, mutation := range []struct {
+		edit func(*ast.FuncDecl) bool
+		name string
+	}{
+		{name: "coalesced stores", edit: coalesceMemoryViewStores},
+		{name: "capture before import", edit: func(function *ast.FuncDecl) bool { return hoistMemoryViewCapture(function, "Xafter_import") }},
+		{name: "capture above loop", edit: func(function *ast.FuncDecl) bool { return hoistMemoryViewCapture(function, "Xloop_tuples") }},
+	} {
+		// Mutate after production validation so source drift checks cannot stand in
+		// for an executable oracle capable of detecting the wrong behavior.
+		write(t, path, string(mutateMemoryView(t, source, mutation.edit)))
+		output, err := runner.Run(ctx, work, goExecutable, "test", "-pgo=off", "-count=1", "-timeout=45s", "./...")
+		if err == nil || !bytes.Contains(output, []byte("--- FAIL: TestMemoryView")) ||
+			!bytes.Contains(output, []byte("memory-view")) || !bytes.Contains(output, []byte("mismatch")) {
+			t.Fatalf("memory-view oracle did not reject %s: %v\n%s", mutation.name, err, output)
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func mutateMemoryView(t *testing.T, source []byte, edit func(*ast.FuncDecl) bool) []byte {
+	t.Helper()
+	files := token.NewFileSet()
+	file, err := parser.ParseFile(files, "module.go", source, parser.ParseComments)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	changed := 0
+	for _, declaration := range file.Decls {
+		if function, ok := declaration.(*ast.FuncDecl); ok && edit(function) {
+			changed++
+		}
+	}
+	if changed != 1 {
+		t.Fatalf("semantic mutation changed %d methods, want one", changed)
+	}
+	var output bytes.Buffer
+	if err := format.Node(&output, files, file); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	return output.Bytes()
+}
+
+func coalesceMemoryViewStores(function *ast.FuncDecl) bool {
+	if function.Name.Name != "Xpublish" {
+		return false
+	}
+	for index := 0; index+1 < len(function.Body.List); index++ {
+		first := memoryViewStore(function.Body.List[index])
+		second := memoryViewStore(function.Body.List[index+1])
+		if first == nil || second == nil {
+			continue
+		}
+		word := func(value ast.Expr) ast.Expr {
+			return &ast.CallExpr{Fun: ast.NewIdent("uint64"), Args: []ast.Expr{value}}
+		}
+		first.Fun = ast.NewIdent("store64")
+		first.Args[2] = &ast.BinaryExpr{X: word(first.Args[2]), Op: token.OR, Y: &ast.BinaryExpr{X: word(second.Args[2]), Op: token.SHL, Y: &ast.BasicLit{Kind: token.INT, Value: "32"}}}
+		function.Body.List = append(function.Body.List[:index+1], function.Body.List[index+2:]...)
+		return true
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+func memoryViewStore(statement ast.Stmt) *ast.CallExpr {
+	expression, ok := statement.(*ast.ExprStmt)
+	if !ok {
+		return nil
+	}
+	call, ok := expression.X.(*ast.CallExpr)
+	if !ok || len(call.Args) != 3 {
+		return nil
+	}
+	name, named := call.Fun.(*ast.Ident)
+	view, viewed := call.Args[0].(*ast.Ident)
+	if !named || name.Name != "store32" || !viewed || !strings.HasPrefix(view.Name, "cocoonMemoryView") {
+		return nil
+	}
+	return call
+}
+
+func hoistMemoryViewCapture(function *ast.FuncDecl, name string) bool {
+	if function.Name.Name != name {
+		return false
+	}
+	var captures []ast.Stmt
+	ast.Inspect(function.Body, func(node ast.Node) bool {
+		block, ok := node.(*ast.BlockStmt)
+		if !ok {
+			return true
+		}
+		kept := make([]ast.Stmt, 0, len(block.List))
+		for _, statement := range block.List {
+			assignment, assigned := statement.(*ast.AssignStmt)
+			if assigned && len(assignment.Lhs) == 1 && len(assignment.Rhs) == 1 {
+				view, viewed := assignment.Lhs[0].(*ast.Ident)
+				memory, selected := assignment.Rhs[0].(*ast.SelectorExpr)
+				if viewed && strings.HasPrefix(view.Name, "cocoonMemoryView") && selected && memory.Sel.Name == "memory" {
+					captures = append(captures, statement)
+					continue
+				}
+			}
+			kept = append(kept, statement)
+		}
+		block.List = kept
+		return true
+	})
+	if len(captures) != 1 {
+		return false
+	}
+	entry := 0
+	for entry < len(function.Body.List) {
+		if _, declaration := function.Body.List[entry].(*ast.DeclStmt); !declaration {
+			break
+		}
+		entry++
+	}
+	function.Body.List = append(function.Body.List[:entry], append(captures, function.Body.List[entry:]...)...)
+	return true
+}

+package wasm
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"encoding/binary"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"fmt"

+type viewEvent struct {
+	Kind   uint32 `json:"kind"`
+	Before uint32 `json:"before"`
+	Pages  uint32 `json:"pages"`
+}
+
+type viewStep struct {
+	Export string      `json:"export"`
+	Trap   string      `json:"trap"`
+	Args   []uint32    `json:"args"`
+	Memory []byte      `json:"memory"`
+	Events []viewEvent `json:"events"`
+	Stack  uint32      `json:"stack"`
+}
+
+type viewHistory struct {
+	Name  string     `json:"name"`
+	Steps []viewStep `json:"steps"`
+}
+
+type viewHost struct {
+	module *Module
+	events []viewEvent
+}
+
+func (host *viewHost) Init(value any) { host.module = value.(*Module) }
+
+func (host *viewHost) Xtouch(kind int32) {
+	memory := *host.module.Xmemory().Slice()
+	host.events = append(host.events, viewEvent{uint32(kind), binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(memory), uint32(len(memory) >> 16)})
+	switch kind {
+	case 0:
+		return
+	case 1:
+	case 2:
+		if host.module.Xmemory().Grow(1, 4) < 0 {
+			panic("fixture import growth failed")
+		}
+	case 3:
+		replacement := bytes.Repeat([]byte{0xde}, len(memory))
+		*host.module.Xmemory().Slice() = replacement
+	default:
+		panic("unsupported fixture import")
+	}
+	memory = *host.module.Xmemory().Slice()
+	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(memory[32:], 0x0a0b0c0d+uint32(len(host.events)))
+}
+
+func invokeView(module *Module, step viewStep) (trap string) {
+	defer func() {
+		if value := recover(); value != nil {
+			if fault, ok := value.(runtime.Error); ok && strings.Contains(fault.Error(), "out of range") {
+				trap = "memory"
+			} else {
+				trap = fmt.Sprintf("%T: %v", value, value)
+			}
+		}
+	}()
+	arg := func(index int) int32 { return int32(step.Args[index]) }
+	switch step.Export {
+	case "publish":
+		module.Xpublish(arg(0), arg(1), arg(2))
+	case "reverse":
+		module.Xreverse(arg(0), arg(1), arg(2))
+	case "copy_tuple":
+		module.Xcopy_tuple(arg(0), arg(1), arg(2))
+	case "mixed_tuple":
+		module.Xmixed_tuple(arg(0), arg(1))
+	case "wrapping_tuple":
+		module.Xwrapping_tuple(arg(0))
+	case "after_import":
+		module.Xafter_import(arg(0), arg(1))
+	case "grow_tuple":
+		module.Xgrow_tuple(arg(0), arg(1))
+	case "loop_tuples":
+		module.Xloop_tuples(arg(0), arg(1), arg(2))
+	case "conditional_tuple":
+		module.Xconditional_tuple(arg(0), arg(1))
+	default:
+		panic("unsupported fixture export")
+	}
+	return trap
+}

+func TestMemoryViewHistories(t *testing.T) {
+	data, err := os.ReadFile("histories.json")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	var histories []viewHistory
+	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &histories); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if len(histories) == 0 {
+		t.Fatal("missing independent memory histories")
+	}
+	for _, history := range histories {
+		t.Run(history.Name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			host := new(viewHost)
+			module := New(host)
+			for index, step := range history.Steps {
+				trap := invokeView(module, step)
+				memory := *module.Xmemory().Slice()
+				if trap != step.Trap || !bytes.Equal(memory, step.Memory) || uint32(module.Xstack_value()) != step.Stack {
+					t.Fatalf("memory-view history mismatch at step %d (%s): trap=%q want=%q memory-equal=%v len=%d/%d stack=%d/%d", index, step.Export, trap, step.Trap, bytes.Equal(memory, step.Memory), len(memory), len(step.Memory), uint32(module.Xstack_value()), step.Stack)
+				}
+				if len(host.events) != len(step.Events) {
+					t.Fatalf("memory-view import history mismatch at step %d: %v/%v", index, host.events, step.Events)
+				}
+				for event, want := range step.Events {
+					if host.events[event] != want {
+						t.Fatalf("memory-view import order mismatch at step %d: %v/%v", index, host.events, step.Events)
+					}
+				}
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

+func TestMemoryViewLogicalLength(t *testing.T) {
+	module := New(new(viewHost))
+	backing := bytes.Repeat([]byte{0xef}, 64)
+	clear(backing[:12])
+	*module.Xmemory().Slice() = backing[:12]
+	step := viewStep{Export: "publish", Args: []uint32{8, 0x11223344, 0x55667788}}
+	if trap := invokeView(module, step); trap != "memory" {
+		t.Fatalf("memory-view logical-length trap mismatch: %q", trap)
+	}
+	if binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(backing[8:]) != 0x11223344 || !bytes.Equal(backing[12:], bytes.Repeat([]byte{0xef}, 52)) || module.Xstack_value() != 49136 {
+		t.Fatal("memory-view logical-length prefix mismatch")
+	}
+}

+func TestMemoryViewHeaderReplacement(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, loop := range []bool{false, true} {
+		t.Run(fmt.Sprintf("loop=%v", loop), func(t *testing.T) {
+			host := new(viewHost)
+			module := New(host)
+			old := *module.Xmemory().Slice()
+			if loop {
+				module.Xloop_tuples(3, 0, 3)
+			} else {
+				module.Xafter_import(3, 80)
+			}
+			memory := *module.Xmemory().Slice()
+			if &old[0] == &memory[0] {
+				t.Fatal("fixture did not replace the header")
+			}
+			if loop {
+				if binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(memory) != 0x11223344 || len(host.events) != 3 {
+					t.Fatal("memory-view loop capture mismatch")
+				}
+				for index, event := range host.events {
+					want := uint32(0x11223344)
+					if index == 0 {
+						want = 0
+					}
+					if event.Before != want {
+						t.Fatal("memory-view loop observation mismatch", host.events)
+					}
+				}
+			} else if binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(memory[80:]) != 0x0a0b0c0e || binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(memory[84:]) != 0x55667788 || binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(old[80:]) != 0 {
+				t.Fatal("memory-view replacement capture mismatch")
+			}
+			if module.Xstack_value() != 49152 {
+				t.Fatal("memory-view replacement restoration mismatch")
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

+func TestMemoryViewGrowthStorage(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, spare := range []bool{false, true} {
+		t.Run(fmt.Sprintf("spare=%v", spare), func(t *testing.T) {
+			module := New(new(viewHost))
+			capacity := 65536
+			if spare {
+				capacity *= 3
+			}
+			backing := make([]byte, 65536, capacity)
+			copy(backing, *module.Xmemory().Slice())
+			*module.Xmemory().Slice() = backing
+			module.Xgrow_tuple(65536, 1)
+			memory := *module.Xmemory().Slice()
+			if (&memory[0] == &backing[0]) != spare {
+				t.Fatal("fixture growth did not exercise requested storage path")
+			}
+			if len(memory) != 131072 || binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(memory[65536:]) != 0x11223344 || binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(memory[65540:]) != 0x55667788 || module.Xstack_value() != 49152 {
+				t.Fatal("memory-view growth capture mismatch")
+			}
+		})
+	}
